ConocoPhillips fell 0.6% today, extending a four-day slide that's wiped out 2.8% since late last week. The immediate driver appears to be escalating U.S. economic pressure on Iran—the Treasury sanctioned a UAE bank branch for Iran-tied transactions, and the Navy is now conducting a blockade of Iranian oil exports. These moves typically tighten global oil supplies and should support prices, but instead crude has drifted lower (U.S. oil at $83.90, down from recent highs), suggesting markets are pricing in either weakening demand or skepticism that the sanctions will hold. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, that mismatch between tightening supply and falling prices is a headwind.

The longer context is mounting geopolitical friction without clear resolution. Iran is calling for diplomacy even as it's being squeezed economically, and Gulf nations are resisting any formal toll scheme for the Strait of Hormuz—a chokepoint through which much of global oil flows. This creates uncertainty rather than the kind of clean supply shock that typically lifts oil stocks; traders may be waiting to see whether sanctions actually constrain supplies or whether negotiations emerge instead.
